models.name: Helmeted Head System (HHS) Model
models.what_it_computes: Whole head–helmet explicit FEA computing skull linear and angular accelerations and interface kinematics at the shell–liner–scalp interfaces

models.name: Brain Deformation (BDM) Model
models.what_it_computes: Anatomically detailed explicit FEA of cranial contents computing element-wise principal strain and strain rate fields and bulk brain rotational kinematics

mechanisms.name: Oblique rigid-anvil impact
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Represents fall or collision with tangential loading; rotational dynamics dominate and are critical for diffuse brain deformation risk

mechanisms.name: Normal compliant-anvil drop
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Represents near-normal head contact to softer surfaces; linear acceleration dominates and challenges skull load paths and liner energy management

deviation.detail: Model risk level reported as "low-medium" with rationale

findings.factor: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU
spans: We designed the validation matrix to reflect the product’s intended exposure profile rather than only standard certification conditions.

The oblique suite uses a rigid flat anvil to elicit strong tangential impulses akin to curb–pavement strikes or lateral glancing blows at speed, with incident angles of 30°, 45°, and 60° that concentrate rotational dynamics and align with reported approach angle distributions in urban riding and micromobility incidents.
findings.span: We designed the validation matrix to reflect the product’s intended exposure profile rather than only standard certification conditions.

findings.factor: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU
spans: We designed the validation matrix to reflect the product’s intended exposure profile rather than only standard certification conditions.

The near-normal suite uses compliant anvils with stiffness–damping characteristics matched to common sports-floor and padding materials, emphasizing axial compression of the liner and the load paths into the skull.

spans: Process controls and traceability covered 127 nightly regression cases for 180 consecutive days with zero unexpected diffs; all artifacts resolve to immutable version tags.

A continuous integration (CI) system executed nightly regression tests comprising 127 cases: element and contact benchmarks; model-scale oblique and normal cases at two severities and two orientations each; and randomized spot checks for parameter drifts.
